title: Budget-Distilled ES-SSM: Cross-Budget Knowledge Distillation for Elastic Spectral State Space Models

contributions.purpose: Enable elastic spectral SSMs to retain accuracy at low spectral budgets during runtime truncation.
contributions.mechanism: A cross-budget KL distillation objective that uses the full-budget forward pass as an in-place teacher to align truncated-budget predictions with full-budget teacher distributions.
contributions.evaluation: Preserves and improves full-budget accuracy (+2.69 pp) while enabling budget-elastic inference with minimal accuracy loss on LRA Text.
contributions.domain: elastic spectral state space models for long-sequence modeling
contributions.source_quote: A cross-budget distillation objective for elastic spectral SSMs that uses the full-budget prediction as an in-place teacher for truncated-budget configurations.

contributions.purpose: Sharply improve accuracy of low-budget (small K) truncated configurations.
contributions.mechanism: In-place teacher distillation encouraging shared low-index spectral channels to approximate the full model's decision boundary at small K.
contributions.evaluation: +22.61 percentage points at K=2 (80.67% vs 58.06%) and +10.96 pp average across low budgets on LRA Text.
contributions.source_quote: Dramatic improvement in low-budget accuracy: +22.61 percentage points at K = 2 and +10.96 pp average across low budgets on LRA Text.

contributions.purpose: Flatten the accuracy-vs-budget curve so a single model performs well across all truncation levels.
contributions.mechanism: Cross-budget distillation that stabilizes accuracy across truncation levels, reducing the minimum viable budget.
contributions.evaluation: Near-flat accuracy (0.53 pp variation from K=2 to K=32) vs 19.39 pp baseline degradation; minimum budget sweet spot reduced from K=12 to K=2 (6x reduction).
contributions.domain: runtime budget adaptation for spectral SSMs
contributions.source_quote: Near-flat accuracy curves (0.53 pp variation from K = 2 to K = 32) compared to 19.39 pp degradation for the baseline, reducing the minimum budget sweet spot from K = 12 to K = 2 (6x reduction).

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our cross-budget distillation approach adapts the inplace distillation concept from elastic networks to the spectral truncation setting.

Elastic Spectral SSMs (ES-SSM) (Song & Wang, 2026) enable runtime budget adaptation through spectral truncation, though they suffer from accuracy degradation at low budgets. Our work addresses this limitation through cross-budget knowledge distillation.
Knowledge distillation has been explored for SSM compression (Shah et al. 2025; Chahine et al. 2025), but not for cross-budget alignment within a single elastic model.
